descriptions.root: The single-asset runtime as its own repository. Working path: AGENTS.md → module names → README_module_<name>.md → the module's own skills → code.
descriptions.Makefile: Entrypoint of everything — per-asset fan-out, JOBS measured from cores and memory, OMP threads pinned to 1 for determinism.
descriptions.docker-compose.yml: One image, two anchors: what every service is, and the one command the dashboard and the assets add.
descriptions.module_data/: Ingest — venue downloads, Lean ZIPs, one canonical DuckDB per asset.
descriptions.module_data/ingest.py: Selects one venue's whole candle per minute into the asset's canonical series (primary-failover, full grid).
descriptions.module_data/lean.py: The Lean-exact raw format — the one external-format boundary; the raw tree is written so a Lean backtest could read it directly.
descriptions.module_data/skills/: The module's own contract: candle canonicalisation, and the acquisition methodology beside it.
descriptions.module_ml/: Research — bars, features, triple-barrier labels, purged walk-forward XGBoost.
descriptions.module_ml/skills/: The module's own contract: the research methodology, equation by equation.
descriptions.module_ml/validation.py: Purged walk-forward splits and the frozen final holdout — the gate of the whole system.
descriptions.module_monitoring/: Presentation of what the runtime modules measured, and the one server that serves it.
descriptions.module_monitoring/serve.py: The one server, two roles: the dashboard, and a container reporting itself.
descriptions.module_monitoring/skills/: The module's own contract: the dashboard conventions, the drawing and the DevOps panel.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_dx/: This drawing: the tracked tree rendered by hand with `make monitoring-dx-update`.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_devops/: The DevOps panel, and the one container that holds the docker socket.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_devops/serv: The Docker Engine over its unix socket: the views, and the three verbs offered for this project's own containers.
descriptions.module_skills/: Repository-wide skills, and the index of the skills each module owns.
descriptions.store_assets_artifacts/: Per-asset artifacts — one folder per ticker, the asset's whole namespace: its database and every research file beside it. The raw tree and the run records are untracked, so this view does not hold them.

descriptions.root: The same tracked tree, read forward: every file and folder seated beside the primitive it would run on or live in — the right column of the mapping table in `module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md`, its primitives drawn as icons with the flows between them, and the rows inside them seated beside them. Described and drawn, built nowhere.
descriptions.image_registry: A container image in a registry (Amazon ECR): `mlops-portfolio-1m-pipeline`, the one runtime package every task runs — built from the tree, carrying the code the bind mount carries today, pulled by the task host.
descriptions.Dockerfile: The recipe of the one image, `mlops-portfolio-1m-pipeline`: a dependency layer today, and a future image carries the code — built from the tree and pushed to the registry beside it.
descriptions.requirements.txt: The image's dependency layer, resolved when the image is built and read by no task at run time.
descriptions.task_host: One Linux container instance (Amazon ECS on Amazon EC2): the one host every asset's runs share. It pulls the image and runs the data-ingest and ml-research tasks the state machine starts, and owns no state — a task builds the asset's files and folders on its disk from the asset's prefix and writes them back whole, and nothing stays after the run. `ASSET` is a namespace, never a host of its own; AWS Fargate would be the same task without the host.
descriptions.docker-compose.yml: One task definition parameterised by `ASSET`, registered with the service that runs it on the host beside it — never a new unit per asset; the anchors are its local spelling, one service per ticker written out so the parameter stays visible.
descriptions.log_streams: Log streams keyed by stage and container, and metrics (Amazon CloudWatch): every task's output and the 1 s samples `record.py` keeps in the run record today, shipped off the host. Absent here — described.
descriptions.data_ingest_task: The data-ingest task (an Amazon ECS Task on the task host): one container run per stage — DownloadMarketData and PublishStatus for data once for the basket, BuildCanonicalData once per asset — that fetches the venues' public endpoints, writes the raw objects, builds the asset's canonical market object and exits, holding nothing between runs.
descriptions.module_data/: The code of the data-ingest task: the venue downloads, the Lean raw format, ingest into the canonical market object and the data status — it travels in the image and runs in the task beside it.
descriptions.module_data/config.py: `TICKERS`, the one definition of the basket, and the descriptors that name the raw and canonical objects; `--tickers <TICKER>` — `ASSET` at the container boundary — is the parameter an asset-scoped run takes.
descriptions.module_data/ingest.py: The BuildCanonicalData state: reads the raw objects under a venue and symbol prefix and writes the canonical market object back whole — the storage → ML-compute line begins at its output.
descriptions.module_data/lean.py: The Lean-exact raw format — the whole of Lean's presence here; the strategy host would read the raw objects in this format directly.
descriptions.module_data/status.py: The PublishStatus state for data: one status object for the whole basket, written by the one-off run and never fanned out.
descriptions.module_data/skills/: The module's own contract travels inside the task's code: a document, not a primitive.
descriptions.asset_store: Object storage with one prefix per asset (Amazon S3): the canonical market object as one versioned object, the parquets and JSONs as artifact objects under the same prefix — `store_assets_artifacts/<TICKER>/` read forward. The asset's whole namespace lives here and on no host.
descriptions.raw_store: Raw objects under a venue and symbol prefix (Amazon S3): one immutable object per UTC day, written Lean-exact so the strategy host could read them as they are; their presence is the rebuild condition's only input today. Here it is `store_raw_1m/`, on disk and untracked, so the development view does not hold it.
descriptions.run_store: Status and run objects in object storage: `store_run_records/<run_id>/`, written by `record.py` from inside whichever task ran the stage and closed by its `--finalise` on the host, read by the reader container; the two status snapshots would live here too — tracked beside the page today, so this picture seats them there. Here it is on disk and untracked.
descriptions.store_assets_artifacts/: The local form of the asset prefixes: one folder per ticker, the tracked README and parameters two of its objects; the store beside it is this folder read forward.
descriptions.store_assets_artifacts/BTC/: The `BTC` prefix: `BTC_research_ohlcv.duckdb` as the one versioned database object — pulled into a task's own disk, one writer at a time, written back whole — with the parquets and JSONs as artifact objects keyed `BTC_<artifact>` beside it.
descriptions.ml_research_task: The ml-research task per `ASSET` (`RunTask` with `ASSET=BTC`, on the same host): one container run per stage from AggregateBars to EvaluateStrategy, and PublishStatus for ML once for the basket, never per asset — pulling the asset's versioned object into its own disk, writing it back whole with the artifacts beside it, and holding nothing between runs.
descriptions.module_ml/: The code of the ml-research task: bars, features, labels, search, model, strategy evaluation and the ML status — it travels in the image and runs in the task beside it, one `ASSET` at a time.
descriptions.module_ml/bars.py: The AggregateBars state, and the one write across the storage → ML-compute line: the three aggregation tables are a pure function of the canonical series, written back into the object the task read.
descriptions.module_ml/config.py: The descriptors that name every artifact object under the asset prefix, built on `artifact_dir()` of `module_data/config.py` and consumed by descriptor everywhere; a future `<prefix>/<ticker>/<version>/` is a rename there, not a redesign here.
descriptions.module_ml/validation.py: The gate of the whole system, and the same gate wherever it runs: purged walk-forward folds and the frozen final holdout are code inside the task, not a primitive.
descriptions.module_ml/status.py: The PublishStatus state for ML: the basket's status object as a fold over completed asset artifacts, and each asset's README as an artifact object under its prefix.
descriptions.module_ml/skills/: The research methodology travels inside the task's code: a document, not a primitive.
descriptions.dashboard_front: Static objects behind a content-delivery front (Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront): the page files and the two snapshots, served to the browser with no process rendering them; the reader container answers beside it.
descriptions.reader_container: A container that stays running, not a static object: the `/containers`, `/runs` and `/devops/*` routes of `serve.py`, reading the run objects and reporting the containers — the one project process on this island; the console beside it is not project code.
descriptions.module_monitoring/: The static dashboard's files — the page, its scripts, the two snapshots — as static objects behind the front beside them; `serve.py`'s routes and `record.py` are the reader container's and the tasks' code.
descriptions.module_monitoring/config.py: Every address the reader knows — the internal port, the service names, the run record's paths — built once here; no code depends on a container name.
descriptions.module_monitoring/serve.py: Three things in one file: every file it serves today is a static object behind the front, its `/containers`, `/runs` and `/devops/*` routes are the reader container that stays running, and its asset role, `/status`, is the resident container — a local mechanism with no primitive.
descriptions.module_monitoring/record.py: Writes the run object from inside whichever task ran the stage; its logs and 1 s samples are the log streams and metrics on the task host's island.
descriptions.module_monitoring/index.html: The page: a static object; no process renders it.
descriptions.module_monitoring/data_status.json: A status object produced by data compute and read by the page — a static object beside the page today, tracked so a fresh clone opens on real numbers; its own prefix is a handful of edits away, listed in the skill's review table.
descriptions.module_monitoring/ml_status.json: A status object produced by ML compute, a fold over completed asset artifacts — a static object beside the page today, the same handful of edits away from its own prefix.
descriptions.module_monitoring/skills/: The page's conventions, this drawing's contract and the panel's travel with the code: documents, not primitives.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_dx/: The repository's view — this drawing, a static object like the page, and not project code.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_devops/: The engine's views — a console, not project code; the socket it holds is a local mechanism with no primitive of its own.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_devops/serv: The one container that holds the docker socket: a console over the local engine's own inventory, a local mechanism.
descriptions.strategy_host: A separate Linux instance running QuantConnect Lean (Amazon EC2): one strategy container — a lean-backtest task, or one that stays running and trades live — reading the raw objects in Lean's own format and the research artifacts under the asset prefix, its brokerage credentials read once from the secrets store when it starts. No Lean runtime, container or dependency exists in this repository. Absent here — described.
descriptions.brokerage_secret: A secret in a secrets store (AWS Secrets Manager): the brokerage credentials the strategy host reads when it starts to trade live. Locally there is none — the venue downloads use public endpoints, and neither the dashboard nor the panel asks for a credential. Absent here — described.
descriptions.state_machine: A state machine whose states are the stages (AWS Step Functions): DownloadMarketData → BuildCanonicalData → AggregateBars → GenerateFeatures → GenerateLabels → SearchHyperparameters → TrainModel → EvaluateStrategy → PublishStatus. It starts each task on the host and sits above every stage and inside none — which is why its flows rise over the picture; the Makefile's `all:` and `ml-all:` are the same order, read locally.
descriptions.event_rule: An event rule and a condition state (Amazon EventBridge, a Step Functions choice): new raw objects → does this asset need its artifacts rebuilt? → yes: run the asset's states from BuildCanonicalData on. Today the condition is the downloaders' day-presence skip and the rerun table of `methodology_ml.md` § 11, read by a human. Absent here — described.
descriptions.Makefile: The local spelling of the state machine beside it: `all:` and `ml-all:` list the state order, the fan-out runs one asset's stages in its container, and nothing here schedules — the developer interface, never a scheduler.
descriptions.module_skills/: Repository-wide skills and the register: they travel with the code and deploy nowhere — not project code, not a primitive, and the contract of every boundary this picture draws.
descriptions.module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md: The mapping table this view draws: its left column is the other view of this page, its right column is these primitives.
descriptions.AGENTS.md: The contract, where every boundary on this picture was decided; it deploys nowhere and governs everything that does.
descriptions.README.md: The overview: the domain drawing, and § Architectural direction, where this stance is stated in one paragraph.
